title: Policy Patterns & Form Library for Cross-Functional Requests
author: Mariana Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose: This page centralizes common policy patterns, standard templates, and approved form flows that teams should use when initiating company-wide actions: access requests, change approvals, data lifecycle operations, procurement and expense approvals, vendor onboarding, and business travel. The goal is to reduce friction, shorten review cycles, and ensure consistent audit evidence across teams.

Scope: Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and embedded partners. Where a procedure references an exemption (security, legal, or regulated customers), follow the additional controls in the referenced related pages.

Owner and escalation
- Document owner: Finance & Legal (Policy Operations).
- Primary approver for templates: Policy Council (Security, Legal, Finance, People Ops).
- Escalation path: policy-ops@redwood.ai -> security@redwood.ai -> legal@redwood.ai.

Contents (quick links)
1) Access & Permissions Request pattern
2) Change Management pattern (infra & app)
3) Data Management lifecycle pattern
4) Procurement & Expense flow + approval matrices
5) Vendor onboarding checklist
6) Travel & business expenses baseline
7) Template library (forms & examples)

1) Access & Permissions Request pattern
Summary: Standardize how role-based and temporary elevated access is requested, approved, and recorded to meet least-privilege and audit requirements.

When to use: New team members, contractors, one-off elevated access for incidents, cross-team service accounts, and emergency access.

Key principles
- Least privilege by default.
- Time-boxed approvals for elevated roles (default 7 days for incident fixes, 30 days for project access).
- Two-person approval for dangerous scopes (modify-production, KMS-admin).
- Automated ticketing and entitlement lifecycle tracking mandatory.

Procedure (step-by-step)
1. Submit an Access Request form (see Template A in the Templates section) describing: resource, minimal role required, business justification, request duration, and owner.
2. Auto-route by resource tag: security-owned paths (KMS, IAM, network) -> Security reviewer; product infra -> Infra lead; apps -> App owner.
3. Reviewer validates justification and suggests scoped alternatives if needed.
4. Approver records approval in the ticket, sets expiry, and if appropriate attaches a runbook or rollback step.
5. On expiry, access is automatically revoked; requestor notified.
6. Quarterly entitlement review: service owners receive a compiled list of active entitlements for recertification.

Thresholds and approvals table:
| Scope category | Examples | Approval required | Timebox default |
|---------------|----------|-------------------|-----------------|
| Low | Read-only dashboards, analytics views | Team lead | 90 days |
| Medium | App-level write, non-prod deploy | App owner + Infra lead | 30 days |
| High | Prod deploy, KMS decrypt, network ACL modify | Security + Manager | 7 days (renewable) |

2) Change Management pattern (infra & app)
Purpose: Ensure operational stability and traceability for changes that affect availability, performance, or security.

Classification
- Standard (non-risk): routine, pre-authorized (e.g., minor config tweaks in non-prod).
- Normal (reviewed): requires scheduled review/approval (e.g., schema migration in staging).
- Emergency: immediate action to restore availability or prevent active compromise. Post-facto review required.

Process summary
- All Normal changes must be created in the Change Request form and include risk assessment, rollback plan, owner, and test plan.
- Changes that cross service boundaries must include an impact matrix and a communication plan.
- Emergency changes must follow the Emergency Change checklist and be entered into the system within 24 hours for retrospective review.

Required fields for Change Request form:
- Title, owner, change window, rollback steps, exposed endpoints, observability metrics to watch, SLOs impacted, approvers, and test checklist.

Approval SLAs
- Standard: auto-approve if within template limits.
- Normal: approver response within 48 hours.
- Emergency: phone + ticket escalation; retrospective review within 72 hours.

3) Data Management lifecycle pattern
Objective: Provide consistent handling rules for data at rest, in transit, and during retention/deletion.

Categories and handling rules
- Public: No restrictions.
- Internal: Default classification for most product telemetry and docs. Encrypt in transit; access by role.
- Restricted: Customer PII, credentials, health/regulated data. Require encryption at rest, strict RBAC, audit logging, and data processing agreements.

Retention and deletion
- Default retention: product logs (90 days), analytics aggregates (365 days), PII per contractual terms.
- Deletion requests use the Data Deletion form and must be entered into the Data Operations queue with owner and retention justification.

Data access review cadence
- Monthly automated reports for service owners listing users and service accounts with access to restricted stores.
- Annual third-party data processing inventory required for compliance teams.

Data export and egress
- Exports of restricted data require a Data Export Approval (Security + Legal). Exports must list destination, recipients, purpose, and retention plan.

4) Procurement & Expense flow + approval matrices
Goal: Streamline purchasing while preserving budget controls and supplier vetting.

Procurement steps summary
1. Use the Purchase Requisition form for > $1,000 purchases. Include justification, GL code, vendor details, and required delivery date.
2. For recurring SaaS contracts, complete the SaaS onboarding questionnaire and legal risk self-assessment.
3. Vendor approval tiers: low-risk (vendor under $25k/year) -> Procurement owner sign-off; medium ($25k–$250k) -> Procurement + Finance review; high (>$250k or regulated supplier) -> Procurement + Finance + Legal and Security.

Expense approvals (employee reimbursements)
- Up to $250: manager approval.
- $250–$2,000: manager + finance.
- > $2,000: manager + finance + finance director.

Payment methods and required artifacts
- P-card use requires monthly reconciliation with receipts.
- Invoice payments require PO number and vendor W-9 or equivalent.

5) Vendor onboarding checklist
Required documents and checks (minimum)
- Completed Vendor Intake form with: legal entity, address, primary contact, and product/service description.
- Financial vetting: reference check, credit check if > $100k exposure.
- Security questionnaire for any vendor with access to restricted data. SOC2/ISO evidence where applicable.
- Contract template checklist: indemnity, data protection addendum, termination rights, SLAs.
- Assign vendor owner for regular vendor reviews.

Periodic review schedule
- Strategic vendors: quarterly performance & risk review.
- Tactical vendors: annual review.

6) Travel & business expenses baseline
Principles
- Reasonable, cost-conscious travel that balances safety and business needs.
- Digital-first approvals for remote work travel; physical receipts required for reimbursement when available.

Approvals and limits
- Domestic economy airfare: manager approval. Premium cabin requires director approval.
- Hotel: mid-range reasonable accommodation; exceptions require pre-approval.
- Meals: per-diem recommended; actuals accepted with receipts.

Expense submission
- Submit within 30 days via the Expense form with receipts and GL code. Late submissions > 60 days require manager justification.

7) Template library (included examples)
- Template A: Access Request form (fields: requester, resource, scope, justification, duration, reviewer group)
- Template B: Change Request form (fields: risk level, rollback, test plan, impact matrix)
- Template C: Purchase Requisition (fields: vendor, cost center, account code, required approvals)
- Template D: Vendor Intake & Security Questionnaire (checklist + certification attestation)
- Template E: Data Export Approval (destination, scope, retention, legal approval)
- Template F: Expense Reimbursement (receipt uploads, GL mapping, manager approval)

Storage and audit artifacts
- All form submissions generate a ticket in the centralized Policy Queue and an associated audit record that is retained per retention policy.
- Template attachments and signed contracts must be archived in the Vendor Vault (link in Related Pages) with access logging enabled.

Governance and continuous improvement
- Quarterly review: Policy Operations reviews usage metrics (turnaround times, rejection reasons) and proposes updates.
- Exceptions: Temporary deviations require Exception Request form and sponsorship by a director-level owner. Exceptions are logged and periodically reviewed.

How to adopt these patterns (practical steps)
1. Product or platform teams should start by mapping their current forms to the templates above.
2. Replace bespoke request flows with the standard forms within 60 days.
3. Submit change requests to policy-ops for any required custom fields or integrations.

Appendix: Quick-form snippets
Template A (Access Request example):
- Requester: [name]
- Resource: [service-name / bucket / project-id]
- Scope: [read/write/admin]
- Purpose: [business justification]
- Duration: [YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD]
- Approver(s): [team lead / security]

Template C (Purchase Requisition snippet):
- Vendor: [name]
- SOW / SKU: [attach file]
- Estimated cost: [$] 
- Budget owner: [name] 
- Req. approvals: [manager, procurement, finance] 

End of document. For implementation questions or to request a custom template integration (Jira/Formstack/Workday), contact policy-ops@redwood.ai.
